Design research · 6 August 2026 · Expo React Native · phone, iPad and web

Password recovery that feels safe

A focused review of Champo’s reset-link request screen: one email field, privacy-preserving feedback, clear recovery and a responsive stadium shell.

SynthesisInputReferencesComparisonProposal

Executive synthesis

Observed fact

One required decision

The supplied reference asks only for the account email, then presents one dominant gold action.

Recommendation

Protect account privacy

Use the same success response whether or not an account exists. Do not expose account membership through copy or timing.

Inference

Trust without clutter

The key-and-envelope emblem, delivery note and support path reduce uncertainty without adding another form step.

Recommendation

Adapt the shell

Use a bounded phone form, a centered tablet composition and Champo’s split visual/form layout on wide screens.

Input analysis

User-supplied reference · embedded locally for offline viewing

Observed fact

Hierarchy

Back navigation and brand lead into a key/email trust emblem, a high-contrast heading, explanation, labeled email field, primary reset-link action, return-to-login action, delivery information and support link.

Inference

The screen is the request stage of a two-stage recovery flow; the password itself is changed only after the email link returns to the app.

What strong guidance does differently

Source-reported claim

OWASP treats reset requests as security-sensitive endpoints, not only forms, and recommends anti-enumeration and abuse controls.

Recommendation

The UI should reinforce this backend posture with generic feedback and avoid showing “user not found” after submission.

Fast, low-friction recovery

RecommendationAutofocus is optional because it immediately opens the keyboard; the email field should instead be the first logical focus target. Preserve typed email on validation errors, enable the primary action only for valid input, and move success feedback into a stable live region.

Risks and anti-patterns

Recommendation

No account enumeration

Never distinguish registered and unregistered addresses in visible feedback.

Recommendation

No decorative obstruction

Stadium and emblem imagery remain inaccessible decoration and cannot reduce field contrast.

Recommendation

No dead end

Keep sign-in and support reachable after success, rate limit or network failure.

Recommendations

P0 · high confidence · low effort

Single strong form

Visible email label, native email metadata, inline validation and a 58px gold action.

P0 · high confidence · medium effort

Responsive auth shell

Reuse the same breakpoint and stadium language as sign-in and email verification.

P1 · medium confidence · low effort

Delivery and support

Explain that delivery can take a few minutes and expose the existing support email.

Proposed experience

Information architecture: back + brand → trust emblem → heading and explanation → email form → primary action → status region → return to sign-in → delivery note → support.

States: pristine, invalid email, submitting, generic success, network/rate-limit error.

Accessibility: visible label, email input purpose, keyboard navigation, text errors, live status feedback, 44px+ actions, decorative icons hidden from assistive technology.

Validation: test invalid email, valid submission, generic success, RTL alignment, keyboard avoidance and widths 390, 768 and 1440px.
